ruleset.name: Clean Code Rules
ruleset.description: The Clean Code ruleset contains rules that enforce a clean code base. This includes rules from SOLID and object calisthenics. Rust behavior: docs/cleancode.md.

rule.name: BooleanArgumentFlag
rule.message: The method {0} has a boolean flag argument {1}, which is a certain sign of a Single Responsibility Principle violation.
rule.description: A boolean flag argument is a reliable indicator for a violation of the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP). You can fix this problem by extracting the logic in the boolean flag into its own type or function.

property.name: exceptions
property.description: Comma-separated enclosing type name list of exceptions

property.name: ignorepattern
property.description: Ignore methods matching this regex. Example: /(^(__construct|get.*Filtered)$)/ or (^(new|create))i

rule.name: ElseExpression
rule.message: The method {0} uses an else expression. Else clauses are basically not necessary and you can simplify the code by not using them.
rule.description: An if expression with an else branch is basically not necessary. You can rewrite the conditions in a way that the else clause is not necessary and the code becomes simpler to read. To achieve this, use early returns, or split the work into smaller functions. Prefer `match` or separate early-return arms over a terminal `else`.

rule.name: IfStatementAssignment
rule.message: Avoid assigning values to variables in if clauses and the like (line '{0}', column '{1}').
rule.description: Assignments in if and while conditions are considered a code smell. In Rust this usually appears as an assignment inside a condition block (e.g. `if { x = foo(); true }`). Prefer binding with `let` / `if let` outside the condition.

rule.name: DuplicatedArrayKey
rule.message: Duplicated array key {0}, first declared at line {1}.
rule.description: Defining another value for the same field in a struct literal overrides the previous field binding in languages that allow it. In Rust, duplicate fields are invalid; this rule still reports them when the syntax tree contains them (catalog parity with phpmd).

rule.name: StaticAccess
rule.message: Avoid using static access to class '{0}' in method '{1}'.
rule.description: Associated-function calls on another type (`Other::make()`) create hard dependencies that are difficult to replace in tests. Prefer injecting behaviour. `Self::…` and snake_case module paths are not flagged. Add commonly used utility types to the exceptions list.

property.name: exceptions
property.description: Comma-separated type name list of exceptions (e.g. Math,String)

property.name: ignorepattern
property.description: Ignore methods matching this regex. Example: (^create)i
